name: Nintendo DS family
summary: Explore Nintendo DS family hardware and the split between flashcard-based homebrew on DS/DS Lite and firmware-independent Memory Pit on every DSi.

specs.cpu: ARM9 at 67 MHz plus ARM7 at 33 MHz (DS/DS Lite); ARM9 at 133 MHz plus ARM7 at 33 MHz (DSi/DSi XL)
specs.storage: None internal on DS/DS Lite; SD card slot and internal system memory on DSi/DSi XL
specs.media: DS game cards and GBA cards on DS/DS Lite; DS game cards and SD card on DSi/DSi XL
specs.display: Two 3.0-inch 256x192 LCDs (DS/DS Lite); two 3.25-inch (XL: 4.2-inch) 256x192 LCDs (DSi/DSi XL)

variants.notes: Model code NTR-001. Backlit 3.0-inch screens. No updatable system menu and no software-only exploit; entry is a slot-1 flashcard.

specs.cpu: ARM9 at 67 MHz, ARM7 at 33 MHz
specs.storage: DS game cards and GBA cards; no internal storage

variants.notes: Model code USG-001. Four screen brightness levels. No updatable system menu; entry is a slot-1 flashcard.

specs.cpu: ARM9 at 67 MHz, ARM7 at 33 MHz
specs.storage: DS game cards and GBA cards; no internal storage

variants.storage: DS game cards; SD card; no GBA slot
variants.notes: Model code TWL-001. Launched 2008-11 in Japan and 2009 elsewhere. DSi games are region-locked; DS games are not. GBA play is emulation (GBARunner2).

specs.cpu: ARM9 at 133 MHz, ARM7 at 33 MHz
specs.storage: SD card slot plus internal system memory

variants.storage: DS game cards; SD card; no GBA slot
variants.notes: Model code UTL-001. Launched 2009-11 in Japan and 2010 elsewhere. Larger screens; same homebrew route as DSi.

specs.cpu: ARM9 at 133 MHz, ARM7 at 33 MHz
specs.storage: SD card slot plus internal system memory

firmware.version: DS and DS Lite: no updatable system menu; DSi: last version 1.4.5U on the US support page (2012-12-11). Last versions for other regions are not confirmed by that source.

homebrew.name: Slot-1 flashcard (R4-class kernel)
homebrew.firmware: No system firmware; boots from cartridge
homebrew.summary: A DS/DS Lite entry point that boots a kernel from a microSD card inserted in a slot-1 flashcard. There is no software-only exploit for these models.

compatibility.note: The DS and DS Lite have no updatable system menu and no software exploit; the flashcard is the entry point. Later DSi firmware and 3DS firmware block many cards, so a card that works on a DS Lite may not boot on a DSi.

requirements: A compatible slot-1 flashcard and microSD card.
A kernel or menu image for the specific card.
warnings: Later DSi firmware and all 3DS firmware block many DS flashcards.
A DS Lite flashcard route is not a DSi route.

homebrew.name: Memory Pit
homebrew.summary: The main entry point for DSi homebrew. It runs on every DSi console regardless of firmware version or region and needs an SD card.

compatibility.note: The DSi guide states homebrew runs on all DSi consoles regardless of firmware version or region; Memory Pit is the guide's main entry point.

requirements: A Nintendo DSi or DSi XL.
An SD card with the Memory Pit payload and homebrew.
The DSi Camera application to trigger the exploit.
warnings: Only the minimal brick risk comes from installing Unlaunch; Memory Pit itself is an entry point.

homebrew.name: Unlaunch
homebrew.summary: Installs a boot-stage menu on the DSi so homebrew can be launched before the stock menu. It is the permanent option after an entry point.

compatibility.note: The DSi guide documents Unlaunch installation and uninstallation; the guide states homebrew runs on all DSi consoles regardless of firmware version or region.

requirements: A working Memory Pit or other DSi entry point.
warnings: Unlaunch and NAND writes are the risky steps; a failed NAND restore needs a hardmod.
Keep an untouched NAND backup before installing.

homebrew.name: hiyaCFW
homebrew.summary: An SD-card-based custom firmware menu for the DSi, booted through Unlaunch. It redirects the system NAND to the SD card.

compatibility.note: Documented by the DS-Homebrew Wiki; requires Unlaunch and an SD card. No exact DSi firmware list is published because the DSi route is firmware-independent.

requirements: A compatible SD card formatted as required by hiyaCFW.
warnings: SD card size and format matter; a wrong format is the usual failed install.
Removing hiyaCFW means deleting SD-card content; the stock menu is untouched by an SD-only setup.

homebrew.name: TWiLight Menu++
homebrew.firmware: DSi firmware-independent; DS/DS Lite use a flashcard kernel
homebrew.summary: An open-source DSi Menu replacement that launches DS, DSi and GBA games. It targets DSi, 3DS and DS flashcards.

compatibility.note: TWiLight Menu++ targets DSi and launches DS, DSi and GBA games; the DSi route is firmware-independent.
On DS/DS Lite, TWiLight Menu++ runs from a slot-1 flashcard kernel rather than from an installed exploit.

requirements: A DSi with Unlaunch or a DS/DS Lite flashcard kernel.
An SD card formatted for TWiLight Menu++.
warnings: SD card size and format matter for TWiLight Menu++.
Do not mix DS-mode and 3DS-mode instructions.

homebrew.name: nds-bootstrap
homebrew.summary: Loads DS games from an SD card on DSi (and 3DS) without a flashcart. DS games are region-free.

compatibility.note: Documented by the DS-Homebrew Wiki; the DSi route is firmware-independent.

requirements: A DSi with Unlaunch or hiyaCFW.
nds-bootstrap installed to the SD card.
warnings: DSi games are region-locked; DS games are region-free.

homebrew.name: GBARunner2
homebrew.summary: Runs Game Boy Advance games on DSi and 3DS. On DSi there is no GBA slot, so this is emulation rather than native play.

compatibility.note: Documented by the DS-Homebrew Wiki; the DSi route is firmware-independent.

requirements: A DSi with Unlaunch or hiyaCFW.
GBARunner2 installed to the SD card and GBA ROM dumps supplied by the user.
warnings: No GBA slot on DSi/DSi XL, so compatibility is limited by emulation.
No games or BIOS files are bundled; use your own legally obtained dumps.

homebrew.name: GodMode9i
homebrew.firmware: No system firmware dependency: it runs from a Slot-1 flashcard on DS/DS Lite or from SD/NAND under DSi homebrew.
homebrew.summary: A full-access file browser for DS and DSi. It dumps DS, DSi and GBA cartridges, restores saves, mounts NitroFS images and edits files, and also runs on the 3DS TWL_FIRM.

compatibility.note: Upstream describes DS, DSi and 3DS TWL_FIRM support; it needs a flashcard or DSi homebrew, not a specific system version.

requirements: A Slot-1 flashcard on DS/DS Lite, or DSi homebrew (Unlaunch or hiyaCFW) on DSi.
An SD card or flashcard microSD for the files you read or write.
warnings: File and save operations can overwrite data; back up before writing to cartridges or NAND.
Cartridge dumping needs the right slot and, on DS/DS Lite, a Slot-2 card for some save operations.
homebrew.availability: Open source; releases published by the project.

homebrew.name: DSLinux
homebrew.firmware: DS and DS Lite are supported; the project says newer models such as DSi and 3DS might work in DS-compatibility mode.
homebrew.summary: A port of Linux to the Nintendo DS and DS Lite, with a shell and text-mode applications. It also runs on some DS emulators.

compatibility.note: Project site names the DS and DS Lite as supported hardware.
Site says newer models might work in DS-compatibility mode; no DSi support is claimed.

requirements: A DS or DS Lite with a homebrew entry point such as a Slot-1 flashcard.
An SD card or flashcard storage for the Linux image.
warnings: DSi and 3DS support is not claimed; treat it as experimental DS-compatibility mode.
Text-mode system with limited memory; it is not a desktop environment.
homebrew.availability: Open source; images published by the project.

officialSupport.summary: DSi system software updates ended at 1.4.5U on the US support page; last versions for other regions are not stated there
